newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday March 20.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The Italian government declared a state of emergengy throughout the country in response to the mass influx of Albanian refugees. The measure, which will allow the government to resort to emergency funding and will remain in force until June 30, is contained in a cabinet decree which also empowers the authorities to repatriate presumed "undesirable" refugees. Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said Italy is ready for intervention if needed. (all).

* Massimo D'Alema, leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), met trade union leader Sergio Cofferati and smoothed over his recent criticism of unions' stand over labour and welfare reform. (all).

* Media tycoon Vittorio Cecchi Gori and state broadcaster RAI reached an agreement over a division of the rights to broadcast domestic soccer matches. Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi, who controls Italy's second television group Mediaset, fiercely criticised the deal (all).
* The Senate approved a package of measures to help ease unemployment after the centre-left government overcame strains with its hard-left allies on how to create more jobs (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi will send today a letter to Prime Minister Romano Prodi with estimates of Italy's public sector borrowing requirement for this year. A quarterly report on state accounts is expected by the end of next week, prompting the government to launch a mini-budget aimed at reducing the country's public deficit (all).

* A report by ISTAT, the national statistics institute, showed that in January Italy's producer prices rose 0.9 percent, unchanged from December, while wholesale prices were up 1.0 percent from a 1.4 percent rise in December (all).

* In a letter to prime minister Romano Prodi, chairman of antitrust authority Giuliano Amato warned against the lack of competition in Italy's petrol market, saying prices were too high compared to the rest of Europe (all).

* In an interview, chairman of France Telecom Michel Bon says his group wants to enter Italy's telecommunications market and adds that he is optimistic over talks with Olivetti about participating in telecoms joint venture Infostrada (La Repubblica).

* The Communist Refoundation party has reportedly reached an agreement with the ruling government coalition over the privatisation process. The hard-left party will stop opposing the sell-off of telecommunication holding company STET provided the government delays the privatisation of electricity utility group Enel and oil giant ENI (Corriere della Sera).
* ENI's units Agip Petroli and IP are expected to be merged in the next few months in order to rationalise its retailing network (all).
* The government's plans to privatise Autostrade, Italy's main motorway operator now ownned by state holding IRI, was approved by the public works commission of the Senate (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
